chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Hammad b. Isa. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad narrated to us from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Jabir b. Abdullah said:

I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) three days before his death: The salutation of God be upon you, O father of the two sweet-smelling basils. I entrust my two basils of this world to you, for soon your two pillars shall collapse, and God is my successor over you.

When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, Ali (peace be upon him) said: This is one of my two pillars which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) told me about.
And when Fatima (peace be upon them both) died, Ali (peace be upon him) said: This is the second pillar which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had mentioned.

key_terms.الريحانتين: The two sweet-smelling basils — referring to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, the Prophet's grandsons
key_terms.خليفتي: My successor, my representative — God's guardianship after the Prophet's passing
key_terms.ركناك: Your two pillars — referring to the Prophet himself and Fatima al-Zahra

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say to Ali about Hasan and Husayn before his death?
ai.summary: Three days before his death, the Prophet addressed Imam Ali as 'the father of the two sweet-smelling basils' (al-Hasan and al-Husayn), entrusting them to his care and foretelling that Ali's two pillars — the Prophet himself and Lady Fatima — would soon collapse. The hadith then records Ali's recognition of this prophecy's fulfillment at the deaths of both the Prophet and Fatima. The metaphor of 'basils' (rayhan) for the Prophet's grandsons is well-attested in hadith literature.
